passage: I'm Samir. In our marketing group project I did almost nothing for two weeks, because Francis always finished things early and I told myself he would cover it. Then, the night before the presentation, I walked into the library and saw Francis with red eyes and three empty tea cups, still fixing my survey section. I felt a sharp pang, half guilt and half shame. I sat down and did the charts I owed. At the presentation the teacher asked who had done the analysis. "Francis did the analysis. I did the charts," I said. It was true, and it was smaller than I had wanted it to be. I'm not proud of the two weeks before it.

qa.q: How many empty tea cups were by Francis in the library?
qa.a: There were three empty tea cups.

qa.q: What did Samir feel when he saw Francis fixing the survey section?
qa.a: Samir felt a sharp pang, half guilt and half shame, at seeing how much Francis was carrying.

qa.q: What did Samir do to put the unfairness right?
qa.a: Samir sat down and did the charts Samir owed, and at the presentation Samir named who did what without claiming more.

qa.q: How might Francis have felt covering the survey section?
qa.a: Francis was tired, with red eyes, and may have felt unfairly loaded even without saying so.

grounding: A groupmate slacks off because others will cover, sees the unfairness, contributes and does not claim extra credit.

passage:
In the college library, Reena had spread the project printouts across the table: forty pages, the group's whole survey report. Simran slid into the chair opposite, late again, holding a coffee.
"I added the references," Simran said.
"You formatted the references," Reena said without looking up. "I wrote the analysis. Arvind did the charts. The presentation is tomorrow."
Simran felt a flush rise. She had been planning to present the findings slide, the most impressive part, because she spoke well in front of people.
She looked at the pages. Most had Reena's handwriting in the margins. She thought about how she'd feel if someone did that to her.
"Reena, I've been coasting," she said quietly. "I'm sorry. What's left?"
Reena looked up, surprised. "The appendix tables. And the conclusion needs rewriting."
"I'll do both tonight. And tomorrow you present the findings. They're yours."
Simran stayed in the library till closing, typing.

qa.q: How many pages was the survey report?
Why did Simran feel a flush rise?
qa.a: She felt ashamed, realising how little she had done while planning to present the most impressive part.
She admitted coasting, apologised, took on the appendix tables and the conclusion, and gave Reena the findings slide.

qa.q: How might Reena feel when Simran offers to do the rest?
qa.a: Surprised and relieved, finally recognised for carrying the analysis.

grounding: Shows slacking off because others will cover, then seeing the unfairness, contributing honestly and not claiming credit at the presentation.

passage:
Tanuja,
I've been meaning to write since the presentation on Friday.
When Professor Das praised the survey design, I said, "Thank you, we worked hard on that." Everyone looked at me, and I kept going as if it was mine. It wasn't. You designed the survey and ran the pilot. I skipped two of our meetings and mostly formatted slides.
I told myself it didn't matter who said thank you. It did. I saw your face.
I've emailed Professor Das to say the survey was your work, and I've copied you in. For the final report, I'll write the literature review and the appendix, the parts I left to you, and send drafts by Wednesday so you can check them.
I'm sorry. I relied on you to cover for me and then took the credit. I won't do that again.
Kunal

qa.q: How does Kunal feel about the presentation?
qa.a: Ashamed and guilty, having accepted credit after doing little.

qa.q: What does Kunal do to make it right?
qa.a: Emails Professor Das to credit Tanuja, and takes on the literature review and appendix with drafts by Wednesday.

qa.q: How might Tanuja have felt at the presentation?
qa.a: Hurt and overlooked, watching Kunal accept praise for Tanuja's work.

grounding: Illustrates free-riding on a groupmate and then claiming credit at the presentation, followed by owning it and contributing honestly.
